name: Bortezomib + Lenalidomide + Dexamethasone (VRd)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: VRd is a cytotoxic/targeted triplet backbone and is not biomarker-restricted for eligibility. Cytogenetic risk (FISH for t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p)/TP53, gain/amp 1q) informs risk stratification (R-ISS/R2-ISS) and whether two-drug maintenance is favored, not access to VRd itself. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Multiple Myeloma, v5.2026.

treatmentSetting: primary therapy for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (both transplant-eligible/HCT candidate and transplant-ineligible/HCT-deferred settings)

premedications.name: Herpes zoster (VZV) antiviral prophylaxis
premedications.notes: proteasome-inhibitor-associated VZV reactivation prophylaxis (e.g., acyclovir/valacyclovir) per institutional practice.

supportiveCare: Bortezomib: monitor for peripheral neuropathy at each visit; consider dose reduction/schedule change for grade 2 or higher; VZV antiviral prophylaxis.
Lenalidomide: VTE thromboprophylaxis (aspirin for standard risk, therapeutic anticoagulation for higher risk) and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen); adjust for renal impairment.
Antiemetics: low to moderate emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle
renal function and electrolytes (lenalidomide renal clearance)

doseModificationRules.text: Reduce dose or change schedule for grade 2 or higher bortezomib peripheral neuropathy per labeling; clinical review.

drugs.name: Bortezomib
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286317). Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 SC on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 21-day cycle (weekly SC dosing). SC route reduces peripheral neuropathy versus IV. Schedule taken exactly as printed; not inferred. Give VZV (herpes zoster) antiviral prophylaxis and monitor for peripheral neuropathy.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74 (Plasma Cell Neoplasms), Table 74.6 (Common Treatment Regimens in Multiple Myeloma), p.1520, line 286317 (VRd: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 SC on days 1, 8, and 15)

drugs.name: Lenalidomide
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286318). Lenalidomide 25 mg PO on days 1 to 14 of a 21-day cycle. Requires VTE thromboprophylaxis (aspirin or anticoagulation) and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen); renal dose adjustment per CrCl.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74, Table 74.6, p.1520, line 286318 (VRd: Lenalidomide 25 mg PO on days 1-14)

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286319). The table gives two source-stated dexamethasone options: 20 mg PO on the day of and the day after bortezomib, OR 40 mg on days 1, 8, 15, and 22. This protocol models the 40 mg weekly option on the in-cycle bortezomib days (1, 8, 15) of the 21-day cycle; day 22 in the source phrase falls on day 1 of the following cycle. Dexamethasone dose is taken exactly as the source prints it, not inferred.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74, Table 74.6, p.1520, line 286319 (VRd: Dexamethasone 20 mg on day of and day after bortezomib, or 40 mg on days 1, 8, 15, and 22)
